column1: # Exceptions to the catalogue's rules (tools/level_catalogue.py, apply_boundaries()): functions whose
# boundaries the rules of docs/build/levels.md ("Counting functions") get wrong, with retail's evidence.
# Each line names a row of the catalogue the rules give and applies at every one of its places:
#   start +N        the function starts N bytes later; the words before it are a linker remnant
#   split +N        two functions, the second starting N bytes in
#   join K          one function with the K entries after it
#   size N          the function is N bytes; the word after it is the linker's 0xCDCDCDCD fill
#   variant LL,...  the places in those levels are a function of their own
#   cut [K/]+A:N[r][o],...  the entry (with the K entries after it) is these pieces: each starts A bytes in and
#                   is N bytes, r for a linker remnant, o for a function of its own though its code equals
#                   another level's; the words no piece takes are padding, fill or data
# NTSC-U (SCUS-973.53): the same corrections as config/levels/boundaries.tsv, in NTSC-U names, each read from the
# NTSC-U disc's words. PAL's func_L31_00460008, func_L33_0035FF90, func_L36_00460038 and func_L39_0059FEF0 need no
# line here: NTSC-U's rules already find those functions whole (31:0045CC18 and 40:0053D730, 28 bytes;
# 33:0035F0B8 in func_L01_0035D848, 152 bytes; 36:0045CB08 in func_L01_004886B8, 12 bytes; 39:0059E288 in frontbin's
# func_00394A20, 276 bytes). PAL's func_L39_0059A7A8 (a switch returning one of six addresses) has no copy on NTSC-U.
